sources.entry: nix-package-manager - Nix is a reproducible package manager alternative to Homebrew, with over 80,000 packages.

summary.one_liner: Nix is a reproducible package manager for Linux and other Unix systems, with documentation and development resources hosted on nixos.org and nix.dev.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Nix as a package manager for Linux and other Unix systems aimed at making package management reliable and reproducible. It points to the Nix manual for reference documentation and to nix.dev for installation instructions and beginner tutorials. It also links to the reference manual for building Nix from source and setting up a development environment, plus a contributing guide. The README gives background on the project: it was created by Eelco Dolstra as part of his PhD thesis and is developed by a community. It lists related projects, namely Nixpkgs, described as a large free software package repository, and NixOS, a Linux distribution configured declaratively. Support channels mentioned are a Discourse forum and Matrix rooms. The metadata's claim of over 80,000 packages is not stated in this README.
use_cases: install reproducible packages on Linux or Unix
alternative to Homebrew for command-line tools
how_to_run: Follow the Nix reference manual to build Nix from source
notable: Purely functional, reproducible package management model from Eelco Dolstra's PhD thesis
Nixpkgs is described as the largest up-to-date free software package repository
NixOS can be configured fully declaratively
Documentation split between the Nix manual and nix.dev tutorials
caveats: README is brief and defers most installation and usage detail to external documentation
Described as a package manager for Linux and other Unix systems; the README does not describe macOS-specific setup
